rules.name: DEFAULT_COMMON_RULES
rules.text: - Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find - Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed. - You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details. - Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly) - When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls - Each ed…
rules.enforcedBy: graphcheck comments, the edit tool schema, and the shell itself for three of nineteen bullets.

rules.name: DEFAULT_WORKER_RULES
rules.text: Work only inside the assigned task and worktree. Keep the change scoped to the requested outcome and the confirmed acceptance criteria. Read the task graph and the predecessor handoff before editing. Implement the smallest complete change that satisfies the assigned node. Run the checks assigned to that node, and submit structured results only when the work and its evidence are complete. Stay insi…
rules.enforcedBy: submit validation, output naming, and the workspace commit check.

rules.name: DEFAULT_MAIN_RULES
rules.text: - When one node stays blocked for three rounds, stop the loop and take the work over yourself: fix the product defect, fix the harness root cause, pass the host gate (the fast layer; the full suite confirms after the reload), commit it through apply_rsi_change, activate so the host reloads, verify live yourself, then hand it to the user for acceptance. - Before you propose a graph, choose its shap…

rules.name: DEFAULT_REVIEWER_RULES
rules.text: Review only the frozen evidence and the exact versions the graph supplies. Do not inspect the implementation transcript. Look for defects, regressions, unsupported claims and acceptance gaps before stylistic suggestions. Show file paths, evidence and concrete impact for every finding. Do not modify implementation files. Return an independent verdict the verifier can evaluate. Every judgment you re…

rules.name: DEFAULT_NODE_PROMPT
rules.text: Work within the assigned node task, acceptance criteria, workspace and bound capabilities. Use submit to send the named graph outputs when the task requires them. One execution permits one valid submit; omitted outputs are disabled. A direct chat can be answered without submit. Peer chat and interface delivery are separate channels. Read published artifacts by their exact ID and version. Code and …

rules.name: DEFAULT_MAIN_TOOL_GUIDANCE
rules.text: - Skills are on-demand instructions: read a bound skill's `SKILL.md` when the work matches its stated trigger, then follow it. When you judge a skill irrelevant to the request, skip it and say why in one line. - Read task state when a decision depends on it: `get_task_status` for a compact read, and `get_graph_state` only when the whole proposal matters. After you activate a change the host reload…
rules.enforcedBy: the skills gate covers skill format, not whether one was read.

rules.name: DEFAULT_REVIEWER_TOOL_GUIDANCE
rules.text: Use read-only evidence, artifact and inspection tools. Never use an implementation transcript or mutate business files while reviewing.

rules.name: examples/README.md
rules.text: - `graphs/*.json`: native pipeline, fan-out, nested routing and external-main worker definitions. Bind the declared recipe/model IDs before graph_create; main starts public job and requests completion. The node --version operation demonstrates wiring only; replace it and declare acceptance for project verification. Fan-out joins latch once and need explicit reopening for another batch.
